2608.06891.title: SkillEval: Decomposing Agent Skill Quality into Interpretable Signals
2608.06891.paper_summary: Agent skills provide reusable procedural knowledge that helps agents solve specialized tasks. As their use expands, evaluating skill quality becomes increasingly important. Existing evaluations often measure skill quality by testing whether a skill improves performance on specific downstream tasks. However, a reusable skill may apply to multiple task scenarios. Downstream evaluation mainly reflects the compatibility between a skill and the evaluated task, provides only a partial view of skill quality, and does not identify which aspect of the skill should be improved. We find that general properties of the \texttt{SKILL.md} document play an important role in skill quality. To evaluate these properties, we propose \textbf{SkillEval}, an interpretable framework for document-level skill evaluation. SkillEval evaluates each property using a fixed and inspectable scoring direction, producing interpretable scores. It further measures and reduces the influence of unrelated document features, such as length and formatting, so that each score captures its intended semantic property more specifically. Specifically, SkillEval learns an interpretable direction for each quality property from controlled positive--negative skill pairs in the hidden representation space of the model, and scores a new skill by projecting its representation onto these fixed directions. We use SkillEval to evaluate skills in controlled quality tests and show that SkillEval reliably distinguishes skills of different quality. In addition, SkillEval scores closely reflect downstream task performance, providing an early indication of whether a skill is likely to help an agent complete a task. We further explore SkillEval for diagnosing weaknesses in skill documents and guiding targeted revisions. The revised skills improve the targeted properties and achieve higher pass rates on downstream tasks.
2608.06891.paper_summary_zh: 代理技能提供可重用的程序性知識，幫助代理解決專門任務。隨著其使用範圍的擴大，評估技能質量變得越來越重要。現有的評估通常通過測試技能是否提高特定下游任務的性能來衡量技能質量。然而，一項可重用的技能可能適用於多個任務場景。下游評估主要反映技能與被評估任務之間的兼容性，只提供技能質量的部分視角，並未確定技能的哪個方面需要改進。我們發現 \texttt{SKILL.md} 文件的一般特性在技能質量中扮演著重要角色。為了評估這些特性，我們提出了 \textbf{SkillEval}，這是一個可解釋的文檔級技能評估框架。SkillEval 使用固定且可檢查的評分方向來評估每個特性，產生可解釋的分數。它進一步測量並減少無關文檔特徵（如長度和格式）的影響，使每個分數更具體地捕捉其預期的語義特性。具體而言，SkillEval 從模型的隱藏表示空間中的受控正負技能對學習每個質量特性的可解釋方向，並通過將其表示投影到這些固定方向上來對新技能進行評分。我們使用 SkillEval 在受控質量測試中評估技能，並顯示 SkillEval 可靠地區分不同質量的技能。此外，SkillEval 的評分與下游任務性能密切相關，提供了技能是否可能幫助代理完成任務的早期指示。我們進一步探索 SkillEval 以診斷技能文檔中的弱點並指導針對性的修訂。修訂後的技能改善了針對性的特性，並在下游任務中達到了更高的通過率。
